items: Zonal Councils are statutory bodies, NOT constitutional bodies, created under the States Reorganisation Act of 1956.
The Chairman of all Zonal Councils is the Union Home Minister, whereas Chief Ministers serve as Vice-Chairman by rotation for one year at a time.
The North-Eastern Council was established under a separate Act (North-Eastern Council Act, 1971) and Sikkim was added as its eighth member in 2002.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Zonal Councils are statutory bodies established by an Act of Parliament (States Reorganisation Act of 1956), not constitutional bodies.
The country is divided into five zones: Northern, Central, Eastern, Western, and Southern Zonal Councils.
The Union Home Minister acts as the common Chairman of all five Zonal Councils.
Chief Ministers of the member states act as Vice-Chairman of the council by rotation for a term of one year at a time.
A separate North-Eastern Council was created under the North-Eastern Council Act of 1971 to address the specific problems of the eight north-eastern states.
